Class SoundInSource

Namespace
SilverCraft.CSCore.Streams
Assembly
SilverCraft.CSCore.dll

Represents an implementation of the IWaveSource interface which provides the data provided by a specified ISoundIn object.

public class SoundInSource : IWaveSource, IReadableAudioSource<byte>, IAudioSource, IDisposable

Constructors

SoundInSource(ISoundIn)

Initializes a new instance of the SoundInSource class with a default bufferSize of 5 seconds.

public SoundInSource(ISoundIn soundIn)

Parameters

soundIn ISoundIn

The soundIn which provides recorded data.

Remarks

Note that soundIn has to be already initialized. Note that old data ("old" gets specified by the bufferSize) gets overridden. For example, if the bufferSize is about 5 seconds big, data which got recorded 6 seconds ago, won't be available anymore.

Initializes a new instance of the SoundInSource class.

soundIn ISoundIn

The soundIn which provides recorded data.

bufferSize int

Size of the internal buffer in bytes.

Remarks

Note that soundIn has to be already initialized. Note that old data ("old" gets specified by the bufferSize) gets overridden. For example, if the bufferSize is about 5 seconds big, data which got recorded 6 seconds ago, won't be available anymore.

FillWithZeros

Gets or sets a value which indicates whether the Read(byte[], int, int) method should always provide the requested amount of data. For the case that the internal buffer can't offer the requested amount of data, the rest of the requested bytes will be filled up with zeros.

Read(byte[], int, int)

Reads a sequence of bytes from the internal stream which holds recorded data and advances the position within the stream by the number of bytes read.

public int Read(byte[] buffer, int offset, int count)

Parameters

buffer byte[]

An array of bytes. When this method returns, the buffer contains the specified byte array with the values between offset and (offset + count - 1) replaced by the bytes read from the current source.

offset int

The zero-based byte offset in the buffer at which to begin storing the data read from the current stream.

count int

The maximum number of bytes to read from the current source.

Returns

int

The total number of bytes read into the buffer.
